newsitem.title: CANADA: Barrick says letter backs its proposal.
newsitem.headline: Barrick says letter backs its proposal.

text.p: Barrick Gold Corp said on Tuesday that the letter it has received from the Indonesian government supports the gold company's proposal to form a joint venture with Bre-X Minerals Ltd to develop the huge Busang gold deposit.
Barrick said it intends to continue discussions with Bre-X to conclude agreements within the one-month deadline set by the government.
"The support for Barrick's participation reflects our unique development capabilities and financial strength," Barrick chief executive Peter Munk said in a statement.
In its letter, the government said it wanted Bre-X and Barrick to form a company and submit new contract of work applications for Busang II and III, Barrick said.

The government confirmed an ownership split for the new company, Barrick said. Barrick "and its partners" will get 67.5 percent, Bre-X "and its partners" will get 22.5 percent and 10 percent will go to the government of Indonesia.
Jakarta also asked the companies to conclude agreements with Bre-X's Indonesian partners and has offered to help facilitate discussions, Barrick said.
The letter recognizes local partners PT Askatindo Karya Mineral and PT Amsya Lyna. They hold a 10 percent interest in the existing contract of work applications for Busang II and III, Barrick said.

"We believe that the Bre-X/Barrick joint venture can satisfy Indonesia's most important objective: the immediate development of Busang in an environmentally responsible manner with economic and social benefits for all concerned," Munk said.
